term_types.name: Reference asset type
term_types.question: What does the asset reference to maintain a stable value?
term_types.description: The corpus distinguishes stablecoins by the asset or basket they are designed to track, which drives classification as e-money token, asset-referenced token, or payment stablecoin. Sources differ on whether a single official currency, a basket, a commodity, or another crypto-asset counts as a valid reference.

values.definition: Stablecoin referencing the value of one official currency, classed as an e-money token under MiCA.

citations.quote: 'electronic money token' or 'e-money token' means a type of crypto-asset that purports to maintain a stable value by referencing the value of one official currency

values.definition: Stablecoin referencing another value or right, or a combination including one or more official currencies, classed as asset-referenced token.

citations.quote: 'asset-referenced token' means a type of crypto-asset that is not an electronic money token and that purports to maintain a stable value by referencing another value or right

values.definition: Crypto-asset whose stability is referenced to a physical commodity such as gold, redeemable for or pegged to commodity value.

citations.quote: redeemable for a predefined amount of a reference asset or assets (eg 1 USD, 1 oz gold)

values.definition: Digital asset obligated to convert or redeem for a fixed amount of monetary value, maintaining stable value relative to it.

citations.quote: is obligated to convert, redeem, or repurchase for a fixed amount of monetary value

values.definition: Stabilisation referencing other crypto-assets or using supply-adjusting protocols; not eligible for the stablecoin classification condition under Basel.

citations.quote: Stabilisation mechanisms that: (i) reference other cryptoassets as underlying assets
purports to maintain a stable value by referencing the value of one official currency
Stablecoins: cryptoasset that aims to maintain a stable value relative to a specified asset, or a pool or basket of assets.

term_types.notes: MiCA splits by single official currency (EMT) vs other references (ART); the GENIUS Act and UK SI 2026/102 use fiat-currency references only, and the UK excludes assets referencing non-fiat assets even if priced in fiat. The FATF and FSB treat any stablecoin, regardless of reference, as covered by the standards.

term_types.name: Issuer identifiability
term_types.question: Is there an identifiable person or entity that issues the crypto-asset?
term_types.description: Several instruments classify crypto-assets by whether a legal or natural person issues them, which determines whether issuer regimes apply. The corpus treats an issuer as the entity that creates or offers the asset, and a token without an identifiable issuer as falling outside issuer-based obligations.

values.definition: A natural or legal person who issues crypto-assets, bringing the asset within issuer obligations.

citations.quote: 'issuer' means a natural or legal person, or other undertaking, who issues crypto-assets

values.definition: Crypto-asset with no identifiable issuer, which MiCA states falls outside its Title II-IV scope.

Crypto-asset issuer An entity, person, or other structure that creates new crypto-assets.

term_types.notes: The US bills define a 'digital asset issuer' by any consideration exchanged and exclude persons who only deploy code issuing end-user distributions; the EU definition is broader and does not exclude that case.

term_types.name: Crypto-asset definitional criteria
term_types.question: Does the digital item meet the criteria to count as a crypto-asset, digital asset or virtual asset?
term_types.description: The corpus defines the core asset category by a set of attributes (digital, DLT-recorded, transferable, storable, usable for payment or investment), and several instruments exclude items that are merely records of other financial assets. Definitions vary in how they treat fungibility, payment or investment purpose, and digital representations of fiat or securities.

values.value: DLT-recorded digital representation of value or right
values.definition: Digital representation of value or rights transferable and storable using DLT or similar technology.

citations.quote: 'crypto-asset' means a digital representation of a value or of a right that is able to be transferred and stored electronically using distributed ledger technology

values.value: payment or investment capable virtual asset
values.definition: Digital representation that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment purposes; excludes fiat and securities representations.

citations.section: Annex A: Recommendation 15, Interpretive Note and FATF Definitions; Glossary

values.definition: Fungible digital representation that can be exclusively possessed and transferred person to person without an intermediary, recorded on a public distributed ledger.

term_types.name: Fungibility
term_types.question: Is the crypto-asset fungible, i.e. interchangeable with other units of the same asset?
term_types.description: Fungibility is used by MiCA to exclude unique assets and by the UK and US definitions to include or exclude assets. NFTs and unique collectibles are treated as a distinct category in several instruments.

This Regulation does not apply to crypto-assets that are unique and not fungible with other crypto-assets.

term_types.notes: FATF treats unique NFTs as generally outside the VA definition unless used for payment or investment in practice; the UK and MiCA both use fungibility as an explicit element.

term_types.name: Economic function of the asset
term_types.question: What is the economic purpose the asset serves: payment, investment, access to a service, or governance?
term_types.description: The corpus classifies tokens by their function (payment, investment, utility access, governance, security), since function determines whether the token falls in MiCA's utility token, financial instrument, or other crypto-asset categories and whether the Howey or MiFID tests apply.

citations.section: Annex A: Recommendation 15, Interpretive Note and FATF Definitions; Glossary
citations.quote: can be used for payment or investment purposes

values.value: digital commodity (intrinsically linked to a blockchain system)
values.definition: US digital asset whose value derives from use of a blockchain system, such as a unit used for fees or incentives.

citations.quote: a digital asset that is intrinsically linked to a blockchain system, and the value of which is derived from or is reasonably expected to be derived from the use of the blockchain system

term_types.name: Native asset versus token standard
term_types.question: Is the crypto-asset native to its own blockchain or a token issued under a smart-contract standard on another chain?
term_types.description: The taxonomy separates assets built on their own chain and governed by its protocol from tokens issued via a smart-contract standard such as ERC-20 or ERC-721. The corpus links the choice of standard to composability and contagion risk.

values.definition: Asset built on its own chain and governed by that chain's protocol rules rather than a token standard.

citations.section: Sections 1-5: motivation, related work, methodology, taxonomy dimensions, dataclass and decision rules, mapping results (summary)
citations.quote: Assets built on their own chain and governed by its own protocol rules rather than a smart-contract token standard

citations.section: Sections 1-5: motivation, related work, methodology, taxonomy dimensions, dataclass and decision rules, mapping results (summary)

term_types.name: Tokenisation form
term_types.question: Is the asset a token that represents ownership or rights in an off-chain or other asset?
term_types.description: Tokenisation is treated as a distinct category: a token representing real-world or traditional assets is classified by the underlying asset, not by the technology. Basel and the US PWG report both make this point.

citations.quote: The regulatory structure of tokenization is determined by what asset is tokenized, not the mere process of tokenizing an asset.

values.definition: Token representing fractional ownership, equity, or a security interest in an off-chain asset or enterprise.

values.value: tokenised physical commodity or precious metal
values.definition: A token representing ownership of a physical commodity, precious metal, or natural resource held in custody or inventory.

values.value: tokenised intellectual property or contractual claim
values.definition: A token representing rights in intellectual property, receivables, debt, or loan-backed equity rather than a physical asset.

citations.quote: Tokenised traditional assets are those assets that are captured within the Basel Framework that are not classified under this chapter as cryptoassets.

citations.quote: The regulatory structure of tokenization is determined by what asset is tokenized, not the mere process of tokenizing an asset.

term_types.notes: Basel defines tokenised traditional assets by the underlying traditional asset class; the US PWG report says tokenised instruments tend to be regulated as securities when the underlying asset is a security.

term_types.name: Wrapped / cross-chain representation
term_types.question: Is the crypto-asset a representation of another asset locked on a different chain or in custody?
term_types.description: Wrapped and bridged tokens are a separate design pattern in the taxonomy: they lock an original asset and mint a copy elsewhere, creating custodial and redemption dependencies.

term_types.name: Source of yield
term_types.question: From what economic activity or protocol mechanism does the holder's return derive?
term_types.description: The taxonomy separates direct yield from underlying economic activity (lending, fees, staking, revenue share) from incentive yield created by token emission, because the source bears on whether profits derive from others' managerial efforts under the Howey test.

values.definition: Return from actual economic activity such as lending interest, liquidity fees, staking rewards or revenue sharing.

term_types.name: Yield distribution mechanism
term_types.question: How is yield delivered to holders: by increasing balance, redemption ratio, price, or another asset?
term_types.description: Yield-bearing assets are classified by how the protocol reflects returns in holder value. This maps to traditional analogues such as pass-through certificates or capitalising share classes.

term_types.description: The taxonomy classifies redemption by where control resides (off-chain issuer, smart contract burn-to-unlock, bridge release, queue, pool claim). Redemption rights are also a criterion in Basel and the US payment stablecoin definitions.
